title: Enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) quantization profile on Hopper runtime with stability hardening
creator: Lucas Chen
description: Goal: Ship a validated FP8 quantization profile for Hopper-class GPUs (H100) supporting E4M3 and E5M2 formats. This ticket covers the runtime enablement, calibration workflow for model-specific ranges, stability fixes (NaN/Inf prevention, scale-clamp heuristics), and accuracy validation against our standard eval suites. Deliverables: (1) FP8 encode/decode kernel selection for Hopper, (2) calibration pipeline and golden dataset, (3) CI coverage + regression checks, (4) rollout plan with safe fallback to INT8/FP16 on regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Quant profiles E4M3 and E5M2 selectable via runtime config flags --quant=fp8:e4m3 or --quant=fp8:e5m2
Accuracy regression <= 0.5% (measured as generation token-level KL/perplexity delta) compared to FP16 baseline across our LLM-generation benchmark suite
Embedding cosine similarity >= 0.995 vs FP16 baseline on embedding benchmark (semantic similarity test set)
No increase in CI crash rate; NaN/Inf occurrences in production telemetry not increased; unit tests for clamp/scale heuristics added
Calibration pipeline (per-channel & per-layer) runs in CI and produces reproducible ranges within 1% on repeated runs
Canary rollout plan approved and automated fallback to INT8/FP16 when per-request quality checks fail
PRs merged: runtime kernels + calibration tooling + CI jobs
technical_decisions: Primary FP8 flavors: E4M3 for compute-heavy layers by default; E5M2 enabled for sensitive layers (attention, layernorm, embedding) where dynamic range is high
Use per-channel min/max (symmetric) quantization for weights and per-tensor dynamic range for activations with stochastic rounding disabled by default
Enable clamp-before-accumulate and NaN-guard paths for Hopper-specific kernels to avoid Inf propagation seen in early runs
Fallback logic: when per-layer calibration variance > 10% or per-request quality check fails, route to INT8 or FP16 depending on cost/latency policy
Calibration algorithm: two-pass histogram-based calibration (coarse global pass, fine per-channel pass) with outlier truncation at 0.1%
calibration_workflow: 1) Collect calibration traces using 10k mixed-length tokens from the golden calibration set (instructions + chat + long context samples). 2) Run coarse global histogram to identify layer-level dynamic range. 3) Run per-channel histogram on weights and per-tensor on activations with 256 bins. 4) Save scale/zero-point and per-layer metadata as profile artifacts. 5) Validate by running validation harness and measuring generation + embedding deltas. Calibration artifacts are stored in s3://redwood-quant/profiles/ENG-4217/<model>/<fp8-profile>.json.
validation_summary: Initial runs on medium-size LLMs (7B/13B) show E4M3 average generation KL delta 0.28% and embedding cosine 0.997. E5M2 applied to attention/query/key/value layers reduced token-level perplexity drift but occasionally triggered underflow for very long sequences; fixed by clamp-before-accumulate and short-sequence scaling heuristics. H100-specific tests revealed a sporadic NaN when running mixed E4M3/E5M2 across micro-batches; root cause traced to a race in shared accumulator initialization and fixed in runtime PR #987. Post-fix validation: no NaNs in 2000 stress runs per model, latency overhead < 2% vs INT8 baseline.
test_matrix: Profiles: FP16 baseline; INT8 baseline; FP8-E4M3; FP8-E5M2; hybrid E5M2 attention + E4M3 rest
GPUs: H100 (PCIe and SXM), CI simulated Hopper environment
Metrics: generation KL/delta-perplexity, embedding cosine, end-to-end latency p50/p95, peak memory, NaN/Inf counts
risks: Primary risks: (1) accuracy regressions on long-context instruction-heavy prompts; (2) sporadic numeric instability on older driver versions; (3) edge-case models with highly skewed weight distributions. Mitigations: block driver versions below 535.x, add calibration variance gating, and provide runtime opt-out flags per-route.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs and run nightly FP8-CI for 72 hours across representative models. 2) Enable canary in staging region with 1% traffic for customers opting in, collect telemetry for 7 days. 3) Expand to 10% with automated QA checks; if drift > thresholds then auto-fallback to INT8. 4) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and signoff from ML-evals team.
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created. Spike initiated to measure baseline FP8 behavior on H100. Lucas and Priya coordinating.
2026-03-03: Collected 10k calibration traces; initial E4M3 run completed. Observed small embedding drift (cosine 0.993).
2026-03-05: Discovered NaN propagation in mixed-profile micro-batches on Hopper. Reproduced locally; root-caused to uninitialized shared accumulator in fused-kernel path.
2026-03-07: Runtime PR #987 created with NaN guard and clamp-before-accumulate. Calibration tooling updated to output per-layer reliability score.
2026-03-09: Calibration pipeline run with two-pass histogram completed. E5M2 on attention reduced perplexity drift but required sequence-length scaling tweak.
2026-03-11: Post-fix stress tests: 2000 runs per model, zero NaNs, KL delta within target for 7B/13B; opening canary prep and CI jobs pending review.
Next: finalize PR reviews, add driver-version gating, and schedule canary for 2026-03-16.
notes: Implementation favored deterministic calibration output (seeded histograms) to ensure CI reproducibility. We opted against stochastic rounding by default because it introduced non-deterministic test flakiness; we will expose it as a runtime knob for research experiments. Also coordinating with support to update KB article on how customers can opt-in/out of FP8 profiles.
